units.heading: 클래스별 책임
units.text: CameraManager는 libcamera의 진입점으로 장치를 열거하고 파이프라인 관리자와 연결하며 애플리케이션에 카메라 접근을 제공합니다. 모든 Camera 객체를 소유하고 핫플러그와 핫언플러그를 처리해 카메라 수명을 관리합니다. 애플리케이션은 한 번에 하나의 관리자 인스턴스만 두어야 하며, 기존 인스턴스를 삭제하기 전에 두 번째 인스턴스를 만들면 동작이 정의되지 않습니다. 관리자는 처음에 중지된 상태이므로 애플리케이션이 start()를 호출해야 하며, 이후 list()와 get()으로 열거된 카메라를 확인하고 가져올 수 있습니다.

units.heading: 클래스별 책임
units.text: Camera는 단일 이미지 소스에서 하나 이상의 이미지 스트림을 생성하는 카메라를 나타내며, 장치 설정과 제어 및 이미지 스트림 캡처를 위한 주요 인터페이스를 제공합니다. 인스턴스는 공유 포인터를 반환하는 create()로 만들어야 하며, 생성자와 소멸자는 비공개이므로 직접 생성하거나 파괴할 수 없습니다. 카메라는 std::shared_ptr<>로 공유되어 마지막 참조가 해제될 때까지 유효하며, 애플리케이션이 보유한 모든 카메라 참조를 해제한 뒤에 CameraManager를 stop()으로 중지할 수 있습니다.

units.heading: 클래스별 책임
units.text: Request는 애플리케이션이 프레임별로 버퍼와 제어 값을 연결해 카메라 장치의 처리를 위해 큐에 넣을 수 있게 합니다. Request::Request()는 애플리케이션용 cookie를 요청에 저장하며, 애플리케이션은 언제든지 cookie()로 이를 확인할 수 있습니다. cookie는 libcamera에 불투명하며, 애플리케이션은 보통 요청 완료 핸들러에서 요청을 외부 리소스에 대응시키는 데 사용합니다.

units.heading: 상태와 허용 호출
units.text: Available 상태에서 acquire()가 성공하면 카메라는 Acquired 상태가 됩니다. configure()가 성공하면 카메라는 Configured 상태가 됩니다. 상태도는 Acquired에서 configure()를 호출하면 Configured로 전이하고, Configured에서 호출하면 같은 상태를 유지한다고 표시합니다. 구현에서는 접근 검사, 설정 검증, 파이프라인 구성과 스트림 확인을 통과한 뒤 상태를 Private::CameraConfigured로 설정하고 0을 반환합니다.

units.heading: 카메라 상태와 허용 호출
units.text: 성공한 상태 전이와 상태를 유지하는 호출을 구분하세요. 상태 변경 함수의 동기화는 호출자가 책임집니다.

units.heading: 카메라 상태와 허용 호출
units.text: 카메라가 Configured 상태에서 start()를 호출하면 Running 상태로 전환합니다. 카메라가 Running 상태일 때 stop()을 호출하면 Stopping 상태로 진입합니다. 정지 처리가 끝나면 카메라는 Stopping 상태에서 Configured 상태로 돌아갑니다. release()가 성공한 뒤 카메라 상태는 Available입니다.

units.heading: 카메라 상태와 허용 호출
units.text: 호출자는 카메라가 Configured 또는 Running 상태일 때만 Camera::createRequest를 호출할 수 있습니다. Camera::queueRequest는 카메라가 Running 상태일 때만 호출할 수 있습니다. 호출자는 카메라가 Configured 상태일 때만 Camera::start()를 호출할 수 있습니다.

units.heading: 카메라 상태와 허용 호출
units.text: Camera 클래스는 카메라 상태에 영향을 주는 함수들을 일반적으로 서로 동기화하지 않습니다. 호출자는 필요한 경우 이 함수들의 동기화를 보장해야 합니다.

units.heading: 오류와 종료
units.text: Camera::queueRequest()는 성공하면 0을, 실패하면 음수 오류 코드를 반환합니다. 카메라가 시스템에서 연결 해제된 경우 -ENODEV, 실행 중이 아닌 경우 -EACCES, 요청이 해당 카메라에 속하지 않는 경우 -EXDEV, 요청이 유효하지 않은 경우 -EINVAL, 요청을 처리할 버퍼 메모리가 없는 경우 -ENOMEM을 반환합니다. Camera::queueRequest()는 요청의 상태가 Request::RequestPending이 아니거나 request->controls().infoMap()이 카메라의 controls() 정보 맵과 다르면 -EINVAL을 반환합니다. 버퍼가 없거나 요청의 버퍼에 연결된 스트림 중 활성 스트림이 아닌 것이 있어도 -EINVAL을 반환합니다.

units.heading: 오류와 종료
units.text: Camera::stop()은 카메라가 실행 중이 아니면 아무 작업 없이 0을 반환합니다. 실행 중이면 접근 검사가 실패할 때 그 오류를 반환하고, 검사를 통과하면 상태를 CameraStopping으로 바꾼 뒤 PipelineHandler::stop을 ConnectionTypeBlocking으로 호출합니다. 이어서 대기 중인 요청이 없다는 단언을 검사하고 상태를 CameraConfigured로 바꾼 뒤 0을 반환합니다. Camera::stop()의 문서에 따르면 이 함수는 캡처와 요청 처리를 즉시 중지하며, 대기 중인 모든 요청을 취소하고 오류 상태로 동기 완료합니다.

units.heading: 동시성과 실행 확인
units.text: Camera::createRequest()는 스레드 안전 함수입니다. Camera::queueRequest()는 스레드 안전 함수입니다. 호출자는 Camera::start와 Camera::stop을 각각 카메라 상태에 영향을 주는 다른 함수와 동기화해야 합니다.

units.heading: 동시성과 실행 확인
units.text: 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeBuffer()와 completeRequest()를 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다. cancelRequest()에는 completeRequest()와 같은 규칙이 적용됩니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 요청이 완료되면 카메라에 알리기 위해 Camera::requestComplete를 호출합니다. 이 함수는 requestCompleted.emit(request)를 호출해 완료된 요청을 애플리케이션에 알리는 신호를 발행합니다.

units.heading: 연결 해제와 대기 요청
units.text: Camera::disconnect()는 하드웨어 연결 해제를 카메라 인스턴스에 알립니다. 먼저 Camera::Private::disconnect()를 호출하며, 이 함수는 상태가 CameraRunning이면 CameraConfigured로 바꾼 뒤 disconnected_를 true로 설정합니다. 그다음 Camera::disconnect()는 애플리케이션에 disconnected 신호를 보냅니다.

units.heading: 연결 해제와 대기 요청
units.text: 연결 해제 알림의 문서는 이후 애플리케이션용 Camera API의 모든 새 호출이 즉시 오류를 반환한다고 설명합니다. 두 Camera::Private::isAccessAllowed() 오버로드는 allowDisconnected가 거짓이고 disconnected_가 참이면 상태를 확인하기 전에 -ENODEV를 반환합니다. 그렇지 않으면 현재 상태가 지정된 상태와 같거나 지정된 범위 안에 있을 때 각각 0을 반환하고, 조건에 맞지 않으면 오류를 기록한 뒤 -EACCES를 반환합니다.

units.heading: 연결 해제와 대기 요청
units.text: 실행 확인 항목: 실행 중 연결이 끊어졌을 때 대기 중인 요청을 처리하는 일은 Camera::disconnect() 문서에 TODO로 남아 있습니다.

units.heading: 클래스 관계
units.text: 화살표의 글자는 추출한 관계를 나타내며, 점선은 상속입니다. 화살표는 참조 대상 또는 기반 클래스를 향합니다. 호출 순서를 뜻하지 않습니다.

units.heading: 요청 생성과 완료
units.text: Camera::createRequest()는 새로 만든 빈 요청을 가리키는 포인터를 반환하며, 오류가 발생하면 nullptr을 반환합니다. 반환된 요청의 소유권은 호출자에게 넘어가며, 호출자는 요청을 삭제할 책임이 있습니다. 호출자는 완료 핸들러에서 요청을 삭제하거나 Request::reuse()로 상태를 초기화한 뒤 재사용할 수 있습니다.

units.heading: 요청 생성과 완료
units.text: Request::addBuffer()의 호출자는 한 요청에 스트림당 버퍼를 하나만 연결해야 합니다. 같은 스트림의 버퍼가 이미 요청에 추가되어 있으면 Request::addBuffer()는 -EEXIST를 반환합니다. Request::addBuffer()를 호출하는 쪽은 요청 완료 콜백이 호출될 때까지 전달한 버퍼가 유효하게 유지되도록 해야 합니다.

units.heading: 요청 생성과 완료
units.text: 애플리케이션은 createRequest()로 요청을 할당한 뒤 queueRequest()를 호출하기 전에 캡처 버퍼를 하나 이상 채워야 합니다. 버퍼가 없는 요청은 유효하지 않으며 큐에 들어가지 않고 거부됩니다. Camera::queueRequest()는 request->_d()->camera()가 현재 카메라인 this와 다르면 오류를 기록하고 -EXDEV를 반환합니다.

units.heading: 요청 생성과 완료
units.text: Camera::queueRequest는 먼저 isAccessAllowed(Private::CameraRunning)의 결과가 음수이면 그 값을 반환하고, 요청을 생성한 카메라가 자신과 다르면 -EXDEV를 반환합니다. 이 검사를 통과한 뒤 request->status()가 Request::RequestPending과 일치하지 않으면 -EINVAL을 반환합니다. Camera::queueRequest()는 request->controls().infoMap()이 &controls()와 같지 않으면 오류를 기록하고 -EINVAL을 반환합니다. Camera::queueRequest()는 앞선 접근 상태, 요청의 카메라, 상태 및 제어 목록 검사를 통과한 뒤 buffers()가 비어 있으면 -EINVAL을 반환합니다.

units.heading: 요청 생성과 완료
units.text: Camera::queueRequest()는 activeStreams_.find(stream)의 결과가 activeStreams_.end()와 같으면 해당 스트림이 없다고 판단하고 -EINVAL을 반환합니다. Camera::queueRequest()는 요청을 카메라에 큐에 넣는 데 성공하면 0을 반환하고, 그 외에는 음수 오류 코드를 반환합니다. 요청이 큐에 들어간 후 카메라는 requestCompleted 신호로 요청의 완료를 알립니다.

units.heading: 소유권과 재사용
units.text: Request::addBuffer()는 요청에 버퍼 참조를 저장합니다. 호출자는 요청 완료 콜백이 호출될 때까지 버퍼가 유효한 상태로 유지되도록 해야 합니다. Request::addBuffer()가 성공하면 전달된 유효한 Fence의 소유권이 buffer로 이동합니다. Request::addBuffer()가 실패하면 전달받은 fence의 소유권을 가져가지 않고 fence를 변경하지 않은 그대로 둡니다.

units.heading: 요청과 버퍼를 유지할 기간
units.text: 요청의 소유권은 호출자에게 있습니다. 버퍼 참조를 연결해도 호출자의 버퍼 유지 책임은 계속됩니다.

units.heading: 요청과 버퍼를 유지할 기간
units.text: 버퍼에 연결된 펜스가 신호되지 않으면 요청은 타임아웃 후 실패하며, 펜스는 버퍼에 남아 있습니다. 애플리케이션은 다른 요청에서 버퍼를 재사용하기 전에 FrameBuffer::releaseFence()로 펜스를 회수해야 합니다. Request::reuse()는 ReuseBuffers 플래그가 설정되어 있으면 bufferMap_의 각 기존 버퍼에 대해 buffer->_d()->setRequest(this)를 호출하여 버퍼를 현재 요청에 연결합니다. Request::reuse()는 flags에 ReuseBuffers가 설정된 경우 bufferMap_의 각 기존 버퍼에 현재 요청을 설정한 뒤 그 버퍼를 pending_에 추가합니다.

units.heading: 요청과 버퍼를 유지할 기간
units.text: Request::reuse()는 flags에 ReuseBuffers가 없는 경우 bufferMap_.clear()를 호출해 bufferMap_을 비웁니다. Request::reuse는 이 대입문에서 status_에 RequestPending 상태를 저장합니다. Request::reuse()는 controls_.clear()를 호출해 controls_를 비웁니다. Request::reuse는 metadata_의 clear()를 호출해 메타데이터를 비웁니다.

units.heading: 요청과 버퍼를 유지할 기간
units.text: Request::ReuseBuffers 플래그는 이전에 addBuffer()로 추가한 버퍼를 유지하여 재사용합니다. 버퍼에 연결된 펜스는 재사용하지 않습니다. 펜스를 사용하는 경우에는 Request::ReuseBuffers 플래그를 사용하지 않도록 권고합니다.

units.heading: Responsibilities by class
units.text: CameraManager is the entry point to libcamera: it enumerates devices, associates them with pipeline managers, and provides applications with access to cameras. It owns all Camera objects and manages camera lifetimes by handling hotplug and hot-unplug. An application must have only one manager instance at a time; creating a second instance before deleting the existing one results in undefined behavior. The manager is initially stopped, so the application must call start(), after which it can inspect and obtain the enumerated cameras using list() and get().

units.heading: Responsibilities by class
units.text: Camera represents a camera that produces one or more image streams from a single image source and provides the main interface for device configuration and control and image stream capture. Instances must be created using create(), which returns a shared pointer; the constructor and destructor are private, so instances cannot be created or destroyed directly. The camera is shared via std::shared_ptr<> and remains valid until the last reference is released. After releasing all camera references held by the application, CameraManager can be stopped with stop().

units.heading: Responsibilities by class
units.text: Request allows an application to associate buffers and control values on a per-frame basis and queue them for processing by a camera device. Request::Request() stores an application-provided cookie in the request, which the application can inspect at any time using cookie(). cookie is opaque to libcamera, and the application typically uses it in the request completion handler to associate the request with an external resource.

units.heading: States and allowed calls
units.text: If acquire() succeeds in the Available state, the camera enters the Acquired state. If configure() succeeds, the camera enters the Configured state. The state diagram shows a transition to Configured when configure() is called in Acquired, and no state change when it is called in Configured. In the implementation, after passing access checks, configuration validation, pipeline configuration, and stream checks, the state is set to Private::CameraConfigured and 0 is returned.

units.heading: Camera states and allowed calls
units.text: Distinguish successful state transitions from calls that preserve state. The caller is responsible for synchronizing state-changing functions.

units.heading: Camera states and allowed calls
units.text: When start() is called while the camera is in the Configured state, the camera transitions to the Running state. When stop() is called while the camera is in the Running state, it enters the Stopping state. Once stopping is complete, the camera returns from the Stopping state to the Configured state. After release() succeeds, the camera state is Available.

units.heading: Camera states and allowed calls
units.text: The caller may call Camera::createRequest only when the camera is in the Configured or Running state. Camera::queueRequest may be called only when the camera is in the Running state. The caller may call Camera::start() only when the camera is in the Configured state.

units.heading: Camera states and allowed calls
units.text: The Camera class generally does not synchronize functions that affect camera state with one another. Callers must ensure synchronization of these functions when necessary.

units.heading: Errors and stopping
units.text: Camera::queueRequest() returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure. It returns -ENODEV if the camera has been disconnected from the system, -EACCES if it is not running, -EXDEV if the request does not belong to that camera, -EINVAL if the request is invalid, and -ENOMEM if there is no buffer memory to process the request. Camera::queueRequest() returns -EINVAL if the request's status is not Request::RequestPending or if request->controls().infoMap() differs from the camera's controls() information map. It also returns -EINVAL if there are no buffers or if any stream associated with the request's buffers is not an active stream.

units.heading: Errors and stopping
units.text: If the camera is not running, Camera::stop() returns 0 without doing anything. If it is running, it returns the error if the access check fails; if the check passes, it changes the state to CameraStopping and calls PipelineHandler::stop with ConnectionTypeBlocking. It then checks the assertion that there are no pending requests, changes the state to CameraConfigured, and returns 0. According to the documentation for Camera::stop(), this function immediately stops capture and request processing, cancels all pending requests, and synchronously completes them with an error status.

units.heading: Concurrency and runtime checks
units.text: Camera::createRequest() is a thread-safe function. Camera::queueRequest() is a thread-safe function. The caller must synchronize Camera::start and Camera::stop respectively with other functions that affect the camera state.

units.heading: Concurrency and runtime checks
units.text: The pipeline handler must call completeBuffer() and completeRequest() on the CameraManager thread. The same rules as for completeRequest() apply to cancelRequest(). The pipeline handler calls Camera::requestComplete to notify the camera when a request completes. This function calls requestCompleted.emit(request) to emit a signal notifying the application of the completed request.

units.heading: Disconnection and pending requests
units.text: Camera::disconnect() notifies a camera instance of a hardware disconnection. It first calls Camera::Private::disconnect(), which changes the state to CameraConfigured if it is CameraRunning, then sets disconnected_ to true. Next, Camera::disconnect() sends the disconnected signal to the application.

units.heading: Disconnection and pending requests
units.text: The disconnection notification documentation states that all subsequent new calls to the Camera API for applications immediately return an error. The two Camera::Private::isAccessAllowed() overloads return -ENODEV before checking the state if allowDisconnected is false and disconnected_ is true. Otherwise, they respectively return 0 when the current state equals the specified state or falls within the specified range; if the condition is not met, they log an error and return -EACCES.

units.heading: Request creation and completion
units.text: Camera::createRequest() returns a pointer to a newly created empty request, or nullptr if an error occurs. Ownership of the returned request passes to the caller, who is responsible for deleting it. The caller may delete the request in the completion handler or reset its state with Request::reuse() and reuse it.

units.heading: Request creation and completion
units.text: The caller of Request::addBuffer() must attach only one buffer per stream to a request. If a buffer for the same stream has already been added to the request, Request::addBuffer() returns -EEXIST. The caller of Request::addBuffer() must ensure that the passed buffer remains valid until the request completion callback is called.

units.heading: Request creation and completion
units.text: After allocating a request with createRequest(), the application must populate it with at least one capture buffer before calling queueRequest(). A request without a buffer is invalid and is rejected without being queued. If request->_d()->camera() differs from this, the current camera, Camera::queueRequest() logs an error and returns -EXDEV.

units.heading: Request creation and completion
units.text: Camera::queueRequest first returns the result of isAccessAllowed(Private::CameraRunning) if it is negative, and returns -EXDEV if the camera that created the request is not itself. After these checks pass, it returns -EINVAL if request->status() does not match Request::RequestPending. If request->controls().infoMap() is not equal to &controls(), Camera::queueRequest() logs an error and returns -EINVAL. After passing the preceding checks of access state, the request's camera, state, and control list, Camera::queueRequest() returns -EINVAL if buffers() is empty.

units.heading: Request creation and completion
units.text: If the result of activeStreams_.find(stream) equals activeStreams_.end(), Camera::queueRequest() determines that the stream does not exist and returns -EINVAL. Camera::queueRequest() returns 0 if it successfully queues the request to the camera; otherwise, it returns a negative error code. After the request is queued, the camera signals its completion with the requestCompleted signal.

units.heading: Ownership and reuse
units.text: Request::addBuffer() stores a buffer reference in the request. The caller must ensure that the buffer remains valid until the request completion callback is invoked. If Request::addBuffer() succeeds, ownership of the valid Fence passed to it transfers to buffer. If Request::addBuffer() fails, it does not take ownership of the passed fence and leaves fence unchanged.

units.heading: How long to retain requests and buffers
units.text: The caller owns the request. Attaching a buffer reference preserves the caller's responsibility to keep the buffer valid.

units.heading: How long to retain requests and buffers
units.text: If a fence attached to a buffer is not signaled, the request fails after a timeout, and the fence remains on the buffer. The application must retrieve the fence with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before reusing the buffer in another request. If the ReuseBuffers flag is set, Request::reuse() calls buffer->_d()->setRequest(this) for each existing buffer in bufferMap_ to attach the buffer to the current request. If ReuseBuffers is set in flags, Request::reuse() sets the current request on each existing buffer in bufferMap_ and then adds the buffer to pending_.

units.heading: How long to retain requests and buffers
units.text: Request::reuse() calls bufferMap_.clear() to clear bufferMap_ if flags does not contain ReuseBuffers. In this assignment, Request::reuse stores the RequestPending state in status_. Request::reuse() calls controls_.clear() to clear controls_. Request::reuse calls clear() on metadata_ to clear the metadata.

units.heading: How long to retain requests and buffers
units.text: The Request::ReuseBuffers flag retains buffers previously added with addBuffer() for reuse. Fences associated with the buffers are not reused. When using fences, it is recommended not to use the Request::ReuseBuffers flag.

units.heading: Validity Period of References Returned by buffers
units.text: Before calling buffers(), buffers must be successfully allocated for the stream using allocate(). The buffers returned by buffers() remain valid until free() is called for the same stream or the FrameBufferAllocator instance is destroyed.

units.heading: Distinguishing duplicate allocation from export failure
units.text: In FrameBufferAllocator::allocate, if inserted of try_emplace is false, an error is logged and -EBUSY is returned. FrameBufferAllocator::allocate() stores the return value of exportFrameBuffers() in the variable ret, and if ret is negative, removes the corresponding entry from buffers_ using erase. After the call to exportFrameBuffers, FrameBufferAllocator::allocate returns ret regardless of the sign of ret, outside the if statement that checks the sign of ret.

units.heading: free Stream Lookup and Return Value
units.text: If FrameBufferAllocator::free cannot find the stream, it returns -EINVAL without removing the buffers_ entry. If it finds the stream, it removes the corresponding buffers_ entry and returns 0.

3A: auto exposure (AE, AGC), auto white balance (AWB) and auto focus (AF) together. They are the main algorithms an IPA computes.
AF (Auto Focus): the algorithm that moves the lens to bring the image into focus.
AGC (Automatic Gain Control): the auto-exposure algorithm that sets exposure time and sensor gain for the scene brightness.
ASSERT: libcamera's debug check macro. In debug builds, a false condition logs a fatal message and aborts execution.
AWB (Auto White Balance): the algorithm that estimates the colour temperature of the light and sets per-channel R, G and B gains so that white looks white.
bayer: a colour filter array where each sensor pixel records only one of R, G or B. Raw data in this format needs debayering before every pixel has RGB values.
CCM: means the IPU3 color correction matrix algorithm.
DEBUG: The name of the most verbose diagnostic severity level for logs. Setting the log level environment variable to `DEBUG` produces detailed logs.
DRM (Direct Rendering Manager): A kernel subsystem that manages Linux graphics devices. The DRM pixel format identifies channel layout within a buffer.
DW100: a separate hardware device that corrects distortion by remapping the image according to a coordinate table. It is found in the NXP i.MX8MP and others.
EBUSY: If FrameBufferAllocator::allocate() is called again on a stream that already has buffers allocated, it returns -EBUSY.
EEXIST: Returns the -EEXIST error when the buffer still has an unreleased fence or when a buffer is already registered for the same stream.
EGL: An interface that connects the display, image, and buffer of a graphics API and operating environment. This document addresses the boundary for importing shared buffers as graphics images.

errno: the standard error numbers Linux functions use to report why they failed. libcamera functions return them as negative values. For example, -ENODEV means no device, -EACCES access denied, -EINVAL an invalid argument, -ENOMEM out of memory and -EXDEV a resource that belongs to another object.
ETIMEDOUT: ETIMEDOUT is the error code that indicates the call did not complete because the time limit (2000 ms in this file) was exceeded while waiting for a response during IPC communication.
FBO: refers to the frame buffer object to which a texture is attached.
fence: A synchronization signal indicating when a buffer can be used. A request with a valid fence waits for the signal during preparation. This is different from request completion.
FPS: FPS means frames per second.
GB: means the green B lens shading correction coefficient.
GL: A prefix used for identifiers in the OpenGL family of graphics APIs. The GL format in this document represents the channel composition of a texture.
GR: means the green R lens shading correction coefficient in the lens shading correction table.
HAL (Hardware Abstraction Layer): the layer that lets an operating system drive different vendors' hardware through one interface. This project ultimately targets an in-house Android Camera HAL.

IPA (Image Processing Algorithms): a separate module (.so) holding the image-quality algorithms. It reads the statistics sent by the ISP and computes the ISP settings for the next frame. It is kept apart from libcamera itself so that vendors can ship it without publishing the source.
IPC (Inter-Process Communication): message exchange between separate processes. Unsigned IPA modules run in a separate process, so libcamera calls them over IPC.
IPU (Image Processing Unit): The name of Intel's Image Processing Unit family. Generation numbers are appended to it, as in IPU3 and IPU6.
IPU3 (Intel Image Processing Unit 3): the camera ISP in some Intel laptop processors. libcamera has a Pipeline Handler and an IPA for it.
IPU6: The name of a generation of the Intel Image Processing Unit (IPU) family. This document lists it as a platform supported by the generic (simple) pipeline without a dedicated Pipeline Handler.

ISP (Image Signal Processor): the processing unit that turns the sensor's raw (bayer) data into a usable image. It performs black-level correction, lens shading correction, white balance, debayering and more.
LOG: Uses the category and severity level specified by the caller.

LSC (Lens Shading Correction): correction for lens shading, where the image edges are darker or tinted compared with the centre because of the lens. It multiplies the image by a correction table laid out as a grid.
LUT (Look-Up Table): precomputed results stored in a table and looked up by input value. The LSC correction table is one.
mali-c55: the Arm Mali-C55 camera ISP. libcamera has a Pipeline Handler and an IPA for it.
mojom: the file format that defines the functions and types of an IPA interface. The proxy code is generated from it at build time.
OMM: an external documentation tool whose reading layout and diagram zoom and search rules this site follows. Only the rules were applied; its runner is not used.
Pending: A request state that has not yet changed to complete or cancelled. It does not mean device processing has started; an earlier request in this state can delay later returns.

Pipeline Handler: the libcamera component that finds a hardware platform's media devices (IPU3, RKISP1 and so on), creates cameras, queues requests to the devices and returns completions. There is one per platform.
RAW: RAW is a classification of pixel color encoding and is distinct from StreamRole::Raw, a separate stream role for capturing raw sensor frames.
RK3399: The name of a system-on-chip (SoC) made by Rockchip. This document lists it as a platform supported by the rkisp1 Pipeline Handler.
RKISP1 (Rockchip Image Signal Processor 1): the camera ISP in Rockchip SoCs, the NXP i.MX8MP and others. libcamera has a Pipeline Handler and an IPA for it.
UQ: an unsigned fixed-point format. UQ<m, n> represents a value with m integer bits and n fractional bits.
UVC (USB Video Class): the standard USB webcams follow. libcamera drives these devices with the uvcvideo Pipeline Handler.
V4L2 (Video4Linux2): the Linux kernel API for cameras and video devices. libcamera controls sensors and ISP devices through it.
WSL2 (Windows Subsystem for Linux 2): an environment for running Linux on Windows. This site is built from libcamera compiled and extracted in WSL2.
Debayering: interpolating each pixel's missing colours from its neighbours to turn bayer raw data into an RGB image. Also called demosaicing.

Metadata: Capture information checked alongside image pixels. Request metadata is provided as a ControlList, and FrameMetadata in FrameBuffer contains the capture status, timestamps, the number of bytes used, and so on. Whether the other fields of FrameMetadata are valid depends on the capture status.
Black level: the baseline value a sensor outputs even with no light at all. It is subtracted in the first stage of ISP processing.
Shader: a small program that runs on the GPU. The software ISP can perform debayering and colour correction in GPU shaders.
Software ISP: the libcamera component that does ISP processing on the CPU or GPU for devices without a hardware ISP. The source calls it software_isp and softisp.
Distortion correction: straightening an image bent by the lens. The RKISP1 pipeline does it by loading a coordinate table (vertex map) into the DW100 device.
Control information map: Information describing the controls and ranges available on a camera. The request control list must reference that camera’s information map.
Tuning file: a YAML file with per-sensor and per-platform algorithm parameters (correction tables, colour matrices and so on). The IPA reads it at start-up.

Frame Buffer: A FrameBuffer object that represents the memory region storing image data. It provides the file descriptor, offset, and length of each memory plane, as well as per-frame metadata. The valid scope of the data and metadata varies depending on whether the capture succeeded, failed, or was cancelled.

Proxy: a stand-in object that takes calls through the same interface instead of calling the IPA module directly, and forwards them to the IPA thread or a separate process. It is generated from the mojom definition at build time.
Active stream: A Stream associated with the current camera configuration. A request buffer referring to a stream from another configuration is rejected during submission checks.

units.text: RKISP1 and Mali-C55 each pass a filename consisting of the sensor model name with .yaml appended, along with the fallback name uncalibrated.yaml, to IPAProxy::configurationFile(). IPAProxy::configurationFile() searches using the IPA module name and the requested filename, and returns the path if it finds one. If it does not find a path and the fallback name is empty, it logs an error and returns an empty string. If the fallback name is not empty, it searches using that name and logs the resulting fallback path as a warning.

units.heading: Software ISP input buffer texture format
units.text: createDMABufTexture2D() maps GL_RED and GL_LUMINANCE each to DRM_FORMAT_R8. GL_RG maps to DRM_FORMAT_GR88, and GL_RGBA maps to DRM_FORMAT_ARGB8888. In switch of eGL::createDMABufTexture2D(), the default branch logs the error unhandled GL format and returns -ENODEV. This branch contains no code that assigns a value to the dmabuf_import_failed_ failure flag.

units.heading: Software ISP input buffer texture format
units.text: In createDMABufTexture2D(), if the result of eglCreateImageKHR() is EGL_NO_IMAGE_KHR, it logs eglCreateImageKHR fail at Debug level. It then assigns true to eglImage.dmabuf_import_failed_ and returns -ENODEV. createInputDMABufTexture2D() passes false as the last argument to createDMABufTexture2D(). createOutputDMABufTexture2D() passes true as the last argument.

units.heading: Software ISP input buffer texture format
units.text: createDMABufTexture2D() initializes ret to 0. On a path that did not return in an earlier error branch, if output is true, it calls attachTextureToFBO(eglImage) to attach the texture to the framebuffer and assigns the return value to ret. If output is false, ret retains its initial value of 0, and the function returns ret at the end.

units.heading: Lens shading correction in the software ISP shaders
units.text: The main() in both shaders first normalizes the value by subtracting blacklevel from rgb and dividing by 1.0 - blacklevel. If APPLY_LSC is defined, it then multiplies rgb by the RGB values of lsc_tex multiplied by 4.0. The packed shader uses textureOut as texture coordinates, while the unpacked shader uses center.xy; the 4.0 scale factor is used to convert from UQ<2, 6> to floating point. It then applies awb gain and clamps each channel between 0 and 1, followed by ccm color correction, value clamping and per-channel contrast, and application of gamma, in that order.

units.heading: IPA module selection and execution boundaries
units.text: IPAModule::match returns true when info_.pipelineVersion is greater than or equal to minVersion and less than or equal to maxVersion, and info_.name and name match. If any of these conditions is not satisfied, it returns false.

units.heading: IPA module selection and execution boundaries
units.text: createIPA first looks up the module using module(name, minVersion, maxVersion) and returns nullptr if the module is not found. If the module exists, it creates a T::Threaded proxy when isSignatureValid(m) is true, or a T::Isolated proxy when it is false. If isValid() of the created proxy is false, it logs an error and returns nullptr; if true, it returns the proxy.

units.heading: IPA module selection and execution boundaries
units.text: IPAManager::isSignatureValid returns false if HAVE_IPA_PUBKEY is not enabled. If enabled, it returns false if forceIsolation_ is true; otherwise, it opens the IPA module file in read-only mode. If the file cannot be opened or the mapped data is empty, it returns false. Otherwise, it records the result of pubKey_.verify(data, ipa->signature()) and returns that result.

units.heading: Thread and process boundaries
units.text: The Threaded init template directly calls ipa_->init(), passing the generated parameters. If the return type is not void, it stores the result in _ret and then returns it; if the return type is void, it returns without specifying a value. The init branch calls the IPA's init method and then passes &thread_, the address of the thread_ object, to proxy_.moveToThread.

units.heading: Boundaries between thread calls and IPC calls
units.text: Threaded and Isolated are alternative paths. Whether each API is synchronous or asynchronous depends on its interface declaration.

units.heading: Boundaries between thread calls and IPC calls

units.heading: Boundaries between thread calls and IPC calls
units.text: The Threaded start template branch first sets state_ to ProxyRunning and calls thread_.start(). It then calls ThreadProxy::start through proxy_.invokeMethod() with the ConnectionTypeBlocking connection type and the template's method parameter, and returns the result. In the ordinary synchronous method branch, which is not init, start, or stop, the generated Threaded method directly calls the method of the same name on ipa_ with the parameters it received and returns the result. In the asynchronous method branch, the ASSERT macro checks the state_ == ProxyRunning expression.

units.heading: Boundaries between thread calls and IPC calls
units.text: In the Threaded asynchronous branch, proxy_.invokeMethod uses ConnectionTypeQueued as the connection type when passing the ThreadProxy method. The {{proxy_name}}Threaded constructor calls ipam->load(). If the call returns false, the constructor returns immediately.

units.heading: Boundaries between thread calls and IPC calls
units.text: The {{proxy_name}}Threaded constructor calls ipam->createInterface() if ipam->load() succeeds. If no pointer is returned, it logs an error containing ipam->path() and returns from the constructor.

units.heading: Boundaries between thread calls and IPC calls
units.text: The generated {{proxy_name}}Threaded constructor returns before making connections if ipam->load() fails or ipam->createInterface() returns null. Otherwise, it sets ipa_ and calls proxy_.setIPA(ipa_.get()), then passes the receiver object this and the corresponding event's {{proxy_name}}Threaded::{{method.mojom_name}}Handler method to connect for each IPA event. Connection code is generated for each interface_event.methods entry in the template, after which the constructor sets valid_ to true.

units.heading: Boundaries between thread calls and IPC calls
units.text: The {{proxy_name}}Isolated constructor obtains the worker path using resolvePath("{{module_name}}_ipa_proxy"). If the path is empty, it logs an error and returns. If a path is present, it creates IPCPipeUnixSocket using the IPA module path and the worker path; if it is not connected, it logs an error and returns. Once connected, it connects recv to recvMessage, moves the IPC object to ipc_, and sets valid_ to true.

units.heading: Boundaries between thread calls and IPC calls
units.text: The {{proxy_name}}Isolated constructor returns before the call if the worker path is empty or IPC is not connected. Otherwise, it connects recv of ipc to the {{proxy_name}}Isolated::recvMessage callback of the current object this using connect. The assignment statement for {{proxy_name}}Isolated::{{proxy_name}}Isolated() targets ipc_ and uses std::move(ipc) on the right-hand side. At this point in the code, the {{proxy_name}}Isolated constructor assigns true to valid_.

units.heading: Boundaries between thread calls and IPC calls
units.text: IPAProxy::resolvePath first checks execPaths_ in order, skips empty directories, and returns the first executable worker path. It then checks src/libcamera/proxy/worker in the build path if utils::libcameraBuildPath() is not empty, or the installation directory IPA_PROXY_DIR if it is empty. If it finds an executable worker in the selected directory, it returns its path; otherwise, it returns an empty string.

units.heading: Boundaries between thread calls and IPC calls
units.text: IPCPipeUnixSocket::sendSync calls call with the input payload, response storage location, and cookie from the header, and returns any error returned. call attempts to insert the cookie, response storage location, and completion state into callData_ without checking whether the insertion succeeded. If message transmission fails, it erases the entry at the iterator and returns an error. If transmission succeeds, it starts a 2000 ms timer and processes events on the current thread until completion; if time expires, it erases the entry and returns -ETIMEDOUT. If reception succeeds and readyRead finds a matching cookie in data at least as large as the header, it moves the payload to the corresponding response location and marks it complete. call erases the entry after completion and returns 0, and sendSync creates and stores IPCMessage as the response if out is present, then returns 0.

units.heading: Boundaries between thread calls and IPC calls
units.text: IPCPipeUnixSocket::sendAsync passes data.payload() to socket_->send. If the return value is nonzero, it logs an error and returns that value. If the return value is zero, it returns 0.

units.heading: Frame input and result interfaces
units.text: The [async] method queueRequest of IPAIPU3Interface takes the frame number frame and request control values controls as arguments. computeParams takes frame and bufferId, and processStats takes frame, frameTimestamp, bufferId, and sensorControls. paramsComputed(frame) and metadataReady(frame, metadata) are declared in IPAIPU3EventInterface. setSensorControls takes frame, sensorControls, and lensControls as arguments.

units.heading: Frame input and result interfaces
units.text: The [async] method queueRequest of IPARkISP1Interface takes the frame number frame and request control value reqControls as arguments. computeParams takes frame and bufferId, and processStats takes frame, bufferId, and sensorControls. paramsComputed(frame, bytesused) and metadataReady(frame, metadata) are declared in IPARkISP1EventInterface. setSensorControls takes frame and sensorControls as arguments.

units.heading: IPA objects and shutdown order
units.text: After successfully calling IPAModule::load() once on a valid module, the caller may call createInterface() as many times as needed. createInterface() must not be called on a module that is invalid or has not yet been loaded. load() returns false if the module is invalid and true if it is already loaded; createInterface() returns nullptr if the module is invalid or not loaded, and otherwise calls ipaCreate_().

units.heading: IPA objects and shutdown order
units.text: IPAModule::load() returns false if dlopen() fails. If it cannot find the ipaCreate symbol, it closes the handle, sets it to nullptr, and returns false. On success, it stores the factory, sets loaded_ to true, and returns true.

units.heading: IPA objects and shutdown order
units.text: The Threaded proxy constructor stops if load() fails or createInterface() returns nullptr. If interface creation succeeds, it holds the interface in unique_ptr, sets it in proxy_, connects the event handler, and sets valid_ to true.

units.heading: IPA objects and shutdown order
units.text: Threaded::init() calls the IPA's init, moves proxy_ to thread_, and returns the return value if there is one. start() sets the state to ProxyRunning, starts the thread, and then calls ThreadProxy::start in a blocking manner. The asynchronous method asserts that the state is ProxyRunning, then queues the ThreadProxy method for invocation.

units.heading: IPA objects and shutdown order
units.text: Threaded::stop() asserts that the state is not ProxyStopping and returns if the state is not ProxyRunning. If running, it changes the state to ProxyStopping, calls ThreadProxy::stop in a blocking manner, then requests the thread to exit and waits for it. It then processes this proxy's InvokeMessage messages on the current thread and sets the state to ProxyStopped.

units.heading: IPA objects and shutdown order
units.text: The Isolated proxy constructor aborts if it cannot obtain the worker path or if there is no IPC connection. Once connected, it connects the receive signal to recvMessage, transfers ownership of the IPC object to ipc_, and sets valid_ to true. If ipc_ exists, the destructor asynchronously sends a Exit message containing an increasing sequence number.

units.heading: Creation and IPC failures
units.text: IPAModule::load() returns false if valid_ is false, and returns true if loaded_ is already true. Otherwise, it opens the shared object using dlopen; if that fails, it logs an error and returns false. It then looks up ipaCreate using dlsym; if that fails, it logs an error, calls dlclose, sets dlHandle_ to nullptr, and returns false. If it finds the symbol, it stores it in ipaCreate_, sets loaded_ to true, and returns true.

units.heading: Creation and IPC failures
units.text: IPAModule::createInterface() returns nullptr if the module is invalid or not loaded. If both conditions are satisfied, it calls ipaCreate_() and returns its return value. IPCPipeUnixSocket::sendSync passes the input message's payload and cookie, along with the response storage location, to call. If the return value is nonzero, it logs an error and then returns that value. If call succeeds, it assigns IPCMessage created from the response to *out when out is not null, and returns 0.

units.heading: Creation and IPC failures
units.text: IPCPipeUnixSocket::call inserts an entry into callData_ using cookie, the response pointer, and the completion status false, and retains the resulting iterator iter. It passes message, not the iterator, to the socket's send. If the send result is not 0, it erases the entry pointed to by iter using erase and returns the send result.

units.heading: Creation and IPC failures
units.text: IPCPipeUnixSocket::call uses the iterator iter returned by inserting a response entry, starts the timer with 2000ms, and processes events until iter->second.done becomes true. If the timer is not running while waiting, it erases the entry using callData_.erase(iter) and returns -ETIMEDOUT. Once complete, it erases the entry using the same iterator and returns 0.

units.heading: Reason for separating request submission and completion
units.text: The application must populate the request with at least one capture buffer before calling queueRequest. A request without a buffer is invalid and is rejected without being added to the queue. Once a request is queued, the camera signals its completion through the requestCompleted signal.

units.heading: Reason for separating request submission and completion
units.text: When a pipeline handler calls completeBuffer to signal completion of the last buffer in a request, the request is not completed automatically. This gives the pipeline handler an opportunity to perform any work that may still be needed, and the handler must explicitly complete the request with completeRequest(). Requests are returned to the application in submission order. The pipeline handler may call completeRequest() for completed requests without ordering constraints.

units.text: CameraManager is the entry point to libcamera, enumerating devices, associating them with pipelines, and allowing applications to access cameras in the system. CameraManager::Private::pipelineFactoryMatch creates PipelineHandler using a factory and attempts to match it using an enumerator. If a match is found, it logs the match and tries again; if no match is found, it ends the loop.

units.heading: From device discovery to Camera access
units.text: Only one CameraManager instance must exist at a time. Creating a second instance without first deleting the existing one results in undefined behavior. Once CameraManager::start() has been confirmed to have started, the application can list and use the system's cameras until the camera manager is stopped or the relevant camera is disconnected from the system. Callers must ensure that the manager is running before calling CameraManager::cameras() and CameraManager::get().

units.heading: From device discovery to Camera access
units.text: When the PipelineHandler::match() implementer finds all media devices required for a single pipeline, the implementer must call MediaDevice::acquire() to acquire them all. The implementer must then create one or more corresponding Camera instances, store them internally, and register them with the camera manager.

units.heading: Component responsibilities
units.text: Camera represents a camera that can produce one or more image streams from a single image source and provides the main interface for device configuration and control and image stream capture. Camera is the central object exposed by libcamera. libcamera manages the lifetime of Camera instances using std::shared_ptr<>, and instances must be created using the create() function, which returns a shared pointer. The constructor and destructor of Camera are private to prevent manual creation and destruction.

units.heading: Request creation and ownership
units.text: The caller may call Camera::createRequest() only when the camera is in the Configured or Running state. Ownership of the request returned by Camera::createRequest() passes to the caller, who is responsible for deleting it. Request::reuse() resets the request's state and controls, and when reusing a request instead of creating a new one, the application must call this function before queuing the request to the camera.

units.heading: Capture-session states and resources
units.text: To prepare for capture, the application must acquire and configure the camera, then start it. Once started, the camera can process requests until it is stopped, and the application must release the camera when it has finished using it. The application may start and stop the camera multiple times without releasing it, and may also reconfigure it.

units.heading: Request submission and completion
units.text: The application must populate the request with at least one capture buffer before passing it to Camera::queueRequest(). When the camera finishes processing a request queued with Camera::queueRequest(), it notifies the application of completion through the requestCompleted signal. Camera::queueRequest() must only be called when the camera is in the Running state.

units.heading: Successful submission and capture completion are separate events
units.text: A zero return from queueRequest() reports successful submission. Completion is reported separately by requestCompleted.

units.heading: Buffer completion and request completion
units.text: PipelineHandler::completeBuffer() sends the application a notification that a buffer belonging to the request has completed and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The pipeline handler must explicitly call completeRequest() even after the last buffer has completed.

units.heading: Thread boundaries and synchronization
units.text: The caller must ensure synchronization between functions when necessary when calling functions that affect the state of Camera. The pipeline handler must call PipelineHandler::completeRequest() on the CameraManager thread.

Requests exceeding the limit that have not yet been sent to the hardware remain in an internal pending queue and are sent to the hardware at a later stage.

units.heading: Device matching and object lifetime
units.text: PipelineHandler matches the media device provided by DeviceEnumerator with a pipeline that supports it, and creates and manages the corresponding Camera device. Handler instances use std::shared_ptr<> for reference counting and implement std::enable_shared_from_this<> to create a new std::shared_ptr<> in code paths where only a this pointer is available in a member function. Instances must not be created directly and must always be created through PipelineHandlerFactoryBase::create().

units.heading: Device matching and object lifetime
units.text: If PipelineHandler::match(), called by the camera manager, finds all media devices needed for a single pipeline, it must acquire each one with MediaDevice::acquire(), create one or more Camera instances, store them internally, register them with the camera manager, and then return true. If it does not find all the required devices, it must either refrain from acquiring any devices or release all devices already acquired with MediaDevice::release(), and return false. If there are multiple pipeline instances, each call must acquire the devices required for one instance; if it returns true, a new handler instance is created and match() is called again.

units.heading: Device matching and object lifetime
units.text: PipelineHandler::acquireMediaDevice() searches for an available media device matching the pattern, excluding devices that have already been acquired. If the search or device acquisition fails, it returns nullptr. If successful, it adds the device to an internal list and returns a shared pointer. The caller must not release the returned device directly; the device is released when the handler is destroyed. This function must be called from the CameraManager thread.

units.heading: Device matching and object lifetime
units.text: PipelineHandler::acquire() locks the media devices used by the pipeline to prevent concurrent access by other processes, and they can be acquired recursively within the same process. Each successful acquire() call must be paired with one release() call, and each release() must be paired with a previously successful acquire(). Handlers must not call the two functions directly; the Camera class handles access. Calling release() on a handler that has not acquired the devices results in undefined behavior.

units.heading: Device matching and object lifetime
units.text: PipelineHandler::acquire() locks the media device when useCount_ is 0; if locking fails, it unlocks the device and returns false. If acquireDevice(camera) then fails, it unlocks the device if useCount_ is 0 and returns false; if it succeeds, it increments useCount_ and returns true. PipelineHandler::release() first calls releaseDevice(camera), and if useCount_ is 1, it unlocks the media device and then decrements useCount_.

units.heading: Device matching and object lifetime
units.text: The pipeline handler may override acquireDevice() to handle resources when a camera is acquired, such as opening devices or allocating buffers, and may override releaseDevice() to perform cleanup when a camera is released, such as freeing memory. releaseDevice() is called once for each camera being released, and the handler must not release resources shared by multiple cameras until releaseDevice() has been called for all previously acquired cameras.

units.heading: Configuration inputs and validation duties
units.text: The caller must fill roles with the use cases for which a default configuration is desired. PipelineHandler::generateConfiguration() returns a valid CameraConfiguration if it can satisfy the requested roles, and a null pointer otherwise. The caller can inspect the returned configuration to check the selected streams and default parameters. This function may be called from any thread, must be thread-safe, and must not change the state of camera in the pipeline handler.

units.heading: Configuration inputs and validation duties
units.text: PipelineHandler::configure() is an interface intended to be called by the Camera class, which receives the configuration to be applied from the application, and is called from the CameraManager thread. The configuration is guaranteed to have been validated by CameraConfiguration::validate(), so pipeline handler implementations must not perform additional validation and may use custom fields stored in their own CameraConfiguration derived class. Implementations must associate a Stream instance with each StreamConfiguration entry using StreamConfiguration::setStream(). This function returns 0 on success or a negative error code on failure.

units.heading: Stopping and outstanding requests
units.text: PipelineHandler::stop separates the pending requests in waitingRequests_ by swapping them with the local queue waitingRequests. According to the comment, this prevents pending requests from being requeued when completeRequest() is called inside stopDevice(). Immediately after separating them, it calls stopDevice(camera). After stopDevice() returns, PipelineHandler::stop() takes the separated pending requests from the front one at a time, cancels them, and calls doQueueRequest() for each request.

units.heading: Stopping and outstanding requests
units.text: The stopDevice() implementer must immediately stop capture and request processing for all running streams. The implementer must also cancel all pending requests and immediately complete them with an error status. Finally, PipelineHandler::stop() uses ASSERT to check that queuedRequests_ and waitingRequests_ are empty. It then initializes requestSequence_ to 0.

units.heading: Stopping and outstanding requests
units.text: completeRequest calls doQueueRequests(camera) at the end so that pending requests can be passed to the pipeline.

units.heading: Input Size Search Boundaries in IPU3
units.text: ImgUDevice::calculatePipeConfig() calculates minIfWidth as std::max(in.width - ImgUDevice::kIFMaxCropWidth, ImgUDevice::kIFMaxCropWidth) and minIfHeight as std::max(in.height - ImgUDevice::kIFMaxCropHeight, ImgUDevice::kIFMaxCropHeight). It searches while the width and height are ifWidth >= minIfWidth and ifHeight >= minIfHeight, respectively; in the first search, width is the outer loop, and in the subsequent search, height is the outer loop.

units.heading: Input Size Search Boundaries in IPU3
units.text: ImgUDevice::calculatePipeConfig() returns an empty configuration if in.height is less than ImgUDevice::kIFMaxCropHeight. According to the comment, calculateBDSHeight() crops up to kIFMaxCropHeight lines from the height, so the minimum height wraps if the height falls below that. calculatePipeConfig() sets minIfHeight to max(in.height - ImgUDevice::kIFMaxCropHeight, ImgUDevice::kIFMaxCropHeight) and passes the height to calculateBDS() while the aligned ifHeight is greater than or equal to this value.

units.text: Request::Private::prepare waits until the acquire fence of each frame buffer signals, so that requests to be queued to the hardware device are ready to receive memory transfers. If there are no fences to wait for, it immediately emits the prepared signal; otherwise, it emits the signal when all fences have signaled or the optional timeout expires. If not all fences signal correctly or the optional timeout expires, it cancels the request and emits the Request::prepared signal. units.text: If the indicated condition is true, PipelineHandler::doQueueRequests() executes break to break out of the while loop that processes requests. If prepared_ is false for the leading request in waitingRequests_, doQueueRequests executes break to break out of the while loop. PipelineHandler::doQueueRequest adds request to data->queuedRequests_.

units.text: PipelineHandler::doQueueRequest() assigns the value of requestSequence_ before incrementing it to sequence_. The postfix ++ uses the previous value for the assignment and increments requestSequence_. If request->_d()->cancelled_ is true in doQueueRequest, it calls completeRequest(request) and immediately returns from the function. units.heading: Buffer completion and request return
units.text: PipelineHandler::completeBuffer() notifies the application that a buffer belonging to the request has completed, then updates the request's internal buffer tracking. It returns true if all buffers in the request have completed, or false otherwise. completeBuffer() does not automatically complete the request when the last buffer completes. The pipeline handler must explicitly complete the request by calling completeRequest() separately.

The pipeline handler may call this function for completed requests without ordering constraints.

units.heading: What it does
units.text: libcamera is an open-source library that supports complex cameras for Linux, Android, and ChromeOS. It interfaces with Linux kernel device drivers and provides developers with an intuitive API, reducing the complexity of capturing images with complex cameras on Linux systems.

units.heading: The four layers of the camera stack

units.heading: The four layers of the camera stack
units.text: Userspace is responsible for providing a working camera stack using the driver. Vendors typically implement this individually, and there is no common architecture or API for application developers. Differences between hardware pipelines and their representation in kernel APIs often require custom handling, making the work especially complex.

units.heading: The four layers of the camera stack
units.text: libcamera abstracts the hardware configuration and image control algorithm work performed through kernel APIs to obtain the desired results from cameras on Linux-based systems. This allows developers to work with cameras in a simple, consistent way.

units.heading: The four layers of the camera stack
units.text: At the bottom, kernel drivers control camera hardware and provide a low-level interface to userspace through the Linux kernel's V4L2 API. Above them, the libcamera framework uses its core component, libcamera, to control camera devices and provide a C++ API to higher layers; optional language bindings allow it to connect to other programming languages. The next layer, the libcamera adaptation layer, refers to components that connect other frameworks to libcamera, such as the V4L2 compatibility layer, the gstreamer libcamera element, and the Android camera HAL implementation. Applications and higher-level frameworks at the top are based on the libcamera framework or the adaptation layer and are outside the scope of the libcamera project.

units.heading: Inputs
units.text: The kernel driver controls the camera hardware and provides userspace with low-level interfaces close to the hardware through the Media Controller API, V4L2 Video Device API, and V4L2 Subdev API, which are part of the Linux kernel's V4L2 API family. What this project receives from the lower layer to control the camera has not been confirmed. The Camera Manager, the component that finds and manages cameras, enumerates cameras and creates a Pipeline Handler, the component responsible for camera processing, to manage each Camera supported by libcamera. Only one Camera Manager instance runs per application, ensuring that only one application at a time can control a camera device.

units.heading: Outputs
units.text: An application controls camera devices through the native C++ API provided by libcamera, an interface through which other programs use its functionality. Optional language bindings, which allow access from other programming languages, may also be used. The Camera class, a code unit representing a single camera device, represents a device capable of producing one or more video streams, or continuous flows of images, and provides an API for interacting with the device from configuration through capture.

units.heading: Outputs
units.text: A libcamera adaptation is a general term for a component that connects another framework to libcamera. Examples include the V4L2 compatibility layer, the libcamera element for gstreamer, and an Android camera hardware abstraction layer (HAL) implementation based on libcamera. These components may be in the libcamera project's source code in a separate repository, or they may be moved to the respective projects' repositories.

units.heading: Boundaries with other teams and layers
units.text: Applications and higher-level frameworks based on the libcamera framework (the basic structure of the software) or on an adaptation of libcamera for another environment are outside the scope of the libcamera project. Device manufacturers must contribute device-specific Pipeline Handlers that manage interactions with camera devices directly to libcamera. IPA, an image processing algorithm, is provided as an external plugin called an IPA Module and may be supplied separately by camera manufacturers. IPA Modules included in libcamera are subject to free software licenses, and externally developed IPA Modules may be distributed under closed-source licenses if they do not include libcamera project source code.

units.heading: Caller responsibilities for each validate() result
units.text: If CameraConfiguration::validate() returns CameraConfiguration::Valid, the original configuration was already valid and has not been adjusted. PipelineHandler::generateConfiguration() returns a valid CameraConfiguration if it can satisfy the stream uses requested through roles, and returns a null pointer otherwise. The settings passed to PipelineHandler::configure() are guaranteed to have been validated by CameraConfiguration::validate(), and pipeline handler implementers must not perform additional validation. Implementers of PipelineHandler::configure() must return 0 if configuration succeeds and a negative error code if it fails.

units.heading: Integration sequence and responsibilities
units.text: To prepare for capture, the application must acquire and configure the camera, then start it. After the camera has processed requests and been stopped, the application must release it when it has finished using it. The application may start and stop the camera multiple times without releasing it, and may also reconfigure it. The Camera class generally does not synchronize functions that affect camera state with one another, so the caller must synchronize these functions when necessary. When a PipelineHandler::match() implementer has acquired all media devices required for a single pipeline, the implementer must create and store one or more Camera instances internally and register them with the camera manager.

units.heading: Boundary between hardware and the common layer
units.text: When the PipelineHandler::match() implementer finds all media devices required for a single pipeline, the implementer must acquire each device using MediaDevice::acquire(), then create one or more corresponding Camera instances, store them internally, register them with the camera manager, and return true. If the PipelineHandler::match() implementer cannot find all required media devices and has not yet acquired any devices, the implementer must not acquire any devices. If the implementer has already acquired some, the implementer must call MediaDevice::release() to release all acquired devices and return false. PipelineHandler::match() is called on the CameraManager thread, and when it returns true, a new PipelineHandler instance is created and its match() is called.

units.heading: Configuration interfaces to implement
units.text: The caller of generateConfiguration must populate roles with the use cases for which it wants to obtain a default configuration. The configuration returned by generateConfiguration() contains information about the selected streams and their default parameters. PipelineHandler::generateConfiguration() must return a valid CameraConfiguration if it can satisfy the requested roles, and must return a null pointer otherwise. PipelineHandler::generateConfiguration() may be called from any thread, and the implementation must be thread-safe.

units.heading: Configuration interfaces to implement
units.text: The PipelineHandler::generateConfiguration() implementer must not change the camera state within the pipeline handler. The configuration passed to PipelineHandler::configure() is guaranteed to have been validated by CameraConfiguration::validate(), and pipeline handler implementers must not perform additional validation. The PipelineHandler::configure() implementer must not perform additional validation and may rely on all custom fields stored in its own CameraConfiguration derived class.

units.heading: Configuration interfaces to implement
units.text: When configuring a camera, the implementer of PipelineHandler::configure() must use StreamConfiguration::setStream() to associate a Stream instance with each StreamConfiguration entry in CameraConfiguration. PipelineHandler::configure() is called on the CameraManager thread, and the implementation must return 0 on success and a negative error code on failure.

units.heading: Passing requests to the device and returning them
units.text: When processing a request containing a set of buffers associated with streams and a set of parameters, the queueRequestDevice implementer must configure the device so that those parameters are applied to the frames captured into the buffers supplied in the request. The queueRequestDevice implementer must return 0 on success and a negative error code on failure. PipelineHandler::queueRequestDevice() is called on the CameraManager thread. The pipeline handler must call completeBuffer() on the CameraManager thread to notify the application that a request's buffer has completed and update the request's internal buffer tracking.

units.heading: Passing requests to the device and returning them
units.text: In completeBuffer, even when the last buffer completes, the request does not complete automatically; the pipeline handler must explicitly complete the request using completeRequest(). The pipeline handler must explicitly call completeRequest() to complete the request. The pipeline handler must call completeBuffer from the CameraManager thread.

units.heading: IPA module selection and failure conditions
units.text: When createIPA calls module, it passes name, minVersion, and maxVersion in that order. In the loop, IPAManager::module returns the module.get() of the module for which match first becomes true. The return statement ends the function, so the loop does not continue.

units.heading: IPA module selection and failure conditions
units.text: IPAManager::module iterates over modules_ and returns a pointer to the first module that match the name and minimum and maximum versions. If no module matches, module returns nullptr. createIPA returns nullptr if the search produces no result. The lambda inside createIPA creates a T::Threaded proxy if isSignatureValid(m) is true and a T::Isolated proxy if it is false.

units.heading: IPA module selection and failure conditions
units.text: If the created proxy fails the isValid() check, createIPA logs an error and returns nullptr. If the created proxy passes validation, createIPA returns that proxy.

units.heading: Responsibilities for stopping and handling errors
units.text: PipelineHandler::stop() first executes waitingRequests.swap(data->waitingRequests_) and then calls stopDevice(camera). PipelineHandler::stop() moves all pending requests aside so that they are not requeued when completeRequest() is called inside stopDevice(). The device implementer of stopDevice() must immediately stop capture and request processing for all running streams, cancel all incomplete requests remaining on the device, and immediately complete them with an error status. The common stop() moves waitingRequests_ aside, calls stopDevice(), and then cancels the moved pending requests in order and processes them with doQueueRequest().

units.heading: Responsibilities for stopping and handling errors
units.text: PipelineHandler::stop() collects the pending requests separately, calls stopDevice(), and then cancels each pending request and passes it to doQueueRequest() to assign it a sequence number and temporarily add it to queuedRequests_ so that it is completed in completeRequest(). After processing the pending requests, PipelineHandler::stop() uses two ASSERT to check that queuedRequests_ and waitingRequests_ are empty and stores 0 in requestSequence_.

units.heading: Contracts to check after implementation and execution limits
units.text: Pipeline handler implementers no longer manage the request after completeRequest returns and must not access it. A pipeline handler may pass completed requests to completeRequest without ordering constraints, and this function returns the requests to the application in submission order. The caller must call completeRequest from the CameraManager thread.

units.heading: What it is and whose problem it solves
units.text: libcamera is an open-source library for supporting complex cameras on Linux, Android, and ChromeOS. It connects to Linux kernel device drivers and provides developers with an intuitive API, simplifying the complex task of capturing images with complex cameras on Linux systems. Providing a functioning camera stack using the drivers is the responsibility of user space, and vendors have typically implemented it independently, without a common architecture or API for application developers. This work is complex because hardware pipelines and the way they are represented in kernel APIs vary, often requiring custom handling.

units.heading: The four layers of the camera stack
units.text: libcamera provides a complete camera stack for Linux-based systems. It abstracts the hardware configuration and image control algorithms needed to obtain the desired results from cameras through the kernel's APIs, allowing developers to handle this work in a simple and consistent way. Kernel drivers, the lowest layer of the camera stack, control camera hardware and provide low-level interfaces to user space through the Linux kernel's V4L2 family of APIs. These APIs include Media Controller API, V4L2 Video Device API, and V4L2 Subdev API.

units.heading: The four layers of the camera stack
units.text: The libcamera framework above it is the core layer of the stack. Its core component, libcamera, handles all control of camera devices and provides a native C++ API to higher layers. Optional language bindings allow other programming languages to interface with libcamera.

units.heading: The four layers of the camera stack
units.text: The libcamera adaptation above it is a collective term for components that interface with libcamera from other frameworks. Examples include the V4L2 compatibility layer, the gstreamer libcamera element, and a libcamera-based Android camera HAL implementation. The applications and higher-level frameworks at the top are based on the libcamera framework or a libcamera adaptation. This layer is outside the scope of the libcamera project.

units.heading: Supported hardware and build options
units.text: The documentation lists Arm Mali-C55, Intel IPU3 (ipu3), NXP i.MX8MP (imx8-isi and rkisp1), RaspberryPi 3, 4 and zero (rpi/vc4), and Rockchip RK3399 (rkisp1) as hardware platforms supported by dedicated pipeline handlers. The generic support targets specified in the documentation are USB video device class cameras (uvcvideo), iMX7, IPU6 and Allwinner Sun6i (simple), and a virtual media controller driver for testing (vimc).

units.heading: Supported hardware and build options
units.text: Select the pipeline handlers to build using the array option pipelines. The default is auto, which builds all pipelines applicable to the target architecture. Selecting all builds all pipelines, and if both auto and all are selected, all takes precedence. The individual selection values are imx8-isi, ipu3, mali-c55, rkisp1, rpi/pisp, rpi/vc4, simple, uvcvideo, vimc, and virtual.

units.heading: Capabilities and support scope
units.text: Camera models a camera that can produce one or more image streams from a single image source. It is the central object in libcamera, providing the main interface for configuring and controlling the device and capturing image streams. Once a pipeline handler has matched the required media devices against the devices in the system and can acquire all required devices, it must create the corresponding Camera instances. All PipelineHandler subclasses must be registered with libcamera using the REGISTER_PIPELINE_HANDLER() macro.

units.heading: What device implementers gain from the common layer
units.text: The common PipelineHandler::queueRequest first adds the capture request to an internal pending request list for processing. The request then goes through a preparation process to determine whether it is ready to be queued to the pipeline handler. This function traverses the pending request queue and passes up to maxQueuedRequestsDevice_ ready requests to the pipeline handler in the order they were queued to this function. If a request fails during preparation or the pipeline handler fails to queue it to the hardware, the request is cancelled.

units.heading: What device implementers gain from the common layer
units.text: Tracking queued requests ensures that all requests are automatically completed when the pipeline handler is stopped with stop(), and the pipeline handler must signal request completion with completeRequest(). In contrast, a request is not automatically completed when its last buffer completes in completeBuffer(), so the pipeline handler must explicitly call completeRequest().

units.heading: Device request limits and wait queues
units.text: In the PipelineHandler constructor declaration, the default value of maxQueuedRequestsDevice is 32. maxQueuedRequestsDevice_ limits the number of requests that the pipeline handler must keep queued to the underlying hardware at a time, while the remaining requests wait in an internal pending queue. If the application submits more requests than the device limit, the remaining requests wait in the internal pending queue until they are queued to the hardware later.

units.heading: buffers 반환 참조의 유효기간
units.text: buffers()를 호출하기 전에 해당 스트림에 대해 allocate()로 버퍼를 성공적으로 할당해야 합니다. buffers()가 반환하는 버퍼는 같은 스트림에 대해 free()가 호출되거나 FrameBufferAllocator 인스턴스가 파괴될 때까지 유효합니다.

units.heading: 중복 할당과 내보내기 실패를 구분하기
units.text: FrameBufferAllocator::allocate에서 try_emplace의 inserted가 false이면 오류를 기록하고 -EBUSY를 반환합니다. FrameBufferAllocator::allocate()는 exportFrameBuffers()의 반환값을 변수 ret에 저장하고, ret가 음수이면 buffers_에서 해당 항목을 erase로 제거합니다. FrameBufferAllocator::allocate는 exportFrameBuffers 호출 후 ret의 부호를 검사하는 if문 밖에서 ret의 부호와 관계없이 ret을 반환합니다.

units.heading: free의 스트림 조회와 반환값
units.text: FrameBufferAllocator::free는 스트림을 찾지 못하면 buffers_ 항목을 제거하지 않고 -EINVAL을 반환합니다. 스트림을 찾으면 해당 buffers_ 항목을 제거하고 0을 반환합니다.

3A: 자동 노출(AE·AGC), 자동 화이트 밸런스(AWB), 자동 초점(AF)을 함께 부르는 말입니다. IPA가 계산하는 대표 알고리즘입니다.
AF (Auto Focus): 렌즈 위치를 움직여 초점을 맞추는 알고리즘입니다.
AGC (Automatic Gain Control): 장면 밝기에 맞춰 노출 시간과 센서 게인을 정하는 자동 노출 알고리즘입니다.
ASSERT: libcamera의 디버그 검사 매크로입니다. 디버그 빌드에서 조건이 거짓이면 치명적 로그를 남기고 실행을 중단합니다.
AWB (Auto White Balance): 조명의 색온도를 추정하고, 흰색이 흰색으로 보이도록 R·G·B 채널별 게인을 정하는 알고리즘입니다.
bayer: 센서의 화소마다 R·G·B 중 한 색만 기록하는 색 필터 배열입니다. 이 형식의 원시 데이터는 디베이어를 거쳐야 화소마다 RGB 값을 가집니다.
CCM: IPU3 컬러 교정 행렬 알고리즘을 의미합니다.
DEBUG: 로그의 심각도 수준 중 가장 자세한 진단 정보를 뜻하는 이름입니다. 로그 수준 환경 변수에 `DEBUG`를 지정하면 상세한 로그를 얻습니다.
DRM (Direct Rendering Manager): Linux 그래픽 장치를 관리하는 커널 하위 시스템입니다. DRM 픽셀 형식은 버퍼 안의 채널 배치를 식별합니다.
DW100: 좌표 표에 따라 영상을 다시 배치해 왜곡을 보정하는 별도 하드웨어 장치입니다. NXP i.MX8MP 등에 들어 있습니다.
EBUSY: 이미 버퍼가 할당된 스트림에 대해 FrameBufferAllocator::allocate()를 다시 호출하면 -EBUSY를 반환합니다.
EEXIST: 버퍼에 아직 해제되지 않은 펜스가 남아있거나 동일한 스트림에 이미 버퍼가 등록되어 있을 때 -EEXIST 오류를 반환합니다.
EGL: 그래픽 API와 운영 환경의 디스플레이·이미지·버퍼를 연결하는 인터페이스입니다. 이 문서에서는 공유 버퍼를 그래픽 이미지로 가져오는 경계를 다룹니다.
errno: Linux 함수가 실패 원인을 알리는 표준 오류 번호입니다. libcamera 함수는 이 값을 음수로 돌려줍니다. 예를 들어 -ENODEV는 장치 없음, -EACCES는 접근 거부, -EINVAL은 잘못된 인자, -ENOMEM은 메모리 부족, -EXDEV는 다른 객체에 속한 자원을 뜻합니다.
ETIMEDOUT: ETIMEDOUT는 IPC 통신 과정에서 응답을 기다리는 동안 지정된 시간 (이 파일 기준 2000ms) 이 초과되어 호출이 완료되지 않았음을 나타내는 오류 코드입니다.
FBO: 텍처를 부착할 프레임 버퍼 객체를 의미합니다.
fence: 버퍼를 사용해도 되는 시점을 알리는 동기화 신호입니다. 요청에 유효한 fence가 연결돼 있으면 준비 단계에서 신호를 기다립니다. 요청 완료 신호와는 다릅니다.
FPS: FPS 는 초당 프레임 수를 의미합니다.
GB: 렌즈 음영 보정 표의 녹색 B 음영 계수를 의미합니다.
GL: OpenGL 계열 그래픽 API의 식별자에 쓰이는 접두사입니다. 이 문서의 GL 형식은 텍스처의 채널 구성을 나타냅니다.
GR: 렌즈 음영 보정 표의 녹색 R 음영 계수를 의미합니다.
HAL (Hardware Abstraction Layer): 운영체제가 제조사마다 다른 하드웨어를 같은 인터페이스로 다루게 하는 계층입니다. 이 프로젝트의 최종 적용 대상은 사내 Android Camera HAL입니다.
IPA (Image Processing Algorithms): 화질 알고리즘을 담은 별도 모듈(.so)입니다. ISP가 보낸 통계를 보고 다음 프레임에 쓸 ISP 설정값을 계산합니다. 제조사가 소스를 공개하지 않고 제공할 수 있도록 libcamera 본체와 분리되어 있습니다.
IPC (Inter-Process Communication): 서로 다른 프로세스가 메시지를 주고받는 방식입니다. 서명이 없는 IPA 모듈은 별도 프로세스에서 실행되므로 libcamera가 IPC로 호출합니다.
IPU (Image Processing Unit): Intel의 이미지 처리 장치 계열 이름입니다. IPU3와 IPU6처럼 세대 번호가 붙습니다.
IPU3 (Intel Image Processing Unit 3): 일부 Intel 노트북 프로세서에 들어 있는 카메라 ISP입니다. libcamera에는 이 장치용 Pipeline Handler와 IPA가 있습니다.
IPU6: Intel 이미지 처리 장치(IPU) 계열의 한 세대 이름입니다. 이 문서에서는 전용 파이프라인 핸들러 없이 범용(simple) 파이프라인으로 지원한다고 문서가 적은 플랫폼으로 나옵니다.
ISP (Image Signal Processor): 센서가 출력한 원시(bayer) 데이터를 화면에 쓸 수 있는 영상으로 바꾸는 처리 장치입니다. 블랙 레벨 보정, 렌즈 음영 보정, 화이트 밸런스, 디베이어 등을 수행합니다.
LOG: 호출자가 지정하는 카테고리와 심각도 수준을 사용합니다.
LSC (Lens Shading Correction): 렌즈 특성 때문에 영상 가장자리가 중앙보다 어둡거나 색이 틀어지는 현상(렌즈 음영)을 보정하는 처리입니다. 화면을 격자로 나눈 보정 표를 곱해서 적용합니다.
LUT (Look-Up Table): 계산 결과를 미리 표로 만들어 두고 입력값으로 바로 찾는 방식입니다. LSC 보정 표가 여기에 해당합니다.
mali-c55: Arm Mali-C55 카메라 ISP입니다. libcamera에는 이 장치용 Pipeline Handler와 IPA가 있습니다.
mojom: IPA 인터페이스의 함수와 자료형을 정의하는 파일 형식입니다. 빌드할 때 이 정의로 프록시 코드를 만듭니다.
OMM: 이 사이트의 읽기 화면 배치와 그림 확대·검색 규칙이 참고한 외부 문서 도구입니다. 실행기를 쓰지 않고 규칙만 적용했습니다.
Pending: 아직 완료 또는 취소로 바뀌지 않은 요청 상태입니다. 장치 처리가 시작됐다는 뜻은 아니며, 앞 요청이 이 상태이면 뒤 요청의 반환도 대기할 수 있습니다.
Pipeline Handler: 특정 하드웨어 플랫폼(IPU3, RKISP1 등)의 미디어 장치를 찾아 카메라를 만들고, 요청을 장치에 넣고 완료를 돌려주는 libcamera 구성 요소입니다. 플랫폼마다 하나씩 있습니다.
RAW: RAW는 픽셀의 색상 인코딩 분류이며, 센서의 원시 프레임을 캡처하기 위한 별도의 스트림 역할인 StreamRole::Raw와 구분됩니다.
RK3399: Rockchip이 만든 시스템 반도체(SoC)의 이름입니다. 이 문서에서는 rkisp1 파이프라인 핸들러로 지원한다고 문서가 적은 플랫폼으로 나옵니다.
RKISP1 (Rockchip Image Signal Processor 1): Rockchip SoC와 NXP i.MX8MP 등에 들어 있는 카메라 ISP입니다. libcamera에는 이 장치용 Pipeline Handler와 IPA가 있습니다.
UQ: 부호 없는 고정소수점 형식입니다. UQ<m, n>은 정수부 m비트와 소수부 n비트로 값을 나타냅니다.
UVC (USB Video Class): USB 웹캠이 따르는 표준입니다. libcamera는 이 장치를 uvcvideo Pipeline Handler로 다룹니다.
V4L2 (Video4Linux2): Linux 커널이 카메라와 영상 장치를 다루는 API입니다. libcamera는 이 API로 센서와 ISP 장치를 제어합니다.
WSL2 (Windows Subsystem for Linux 2): Windows에서 Linux를 실행하는 환경입니다. 이 사이트는 libcamera를 WSL2에서 빌드하고 추출한 결과로 만듭니다.
디베이어: bayer 원시 데이터에서 화소마다 빠진 색을 주변 화소로 보간해 RGB 영상을 만드는 처리입니다. 디모자이크라고도 합니다.
메타데이터: 영상 픽셀과 함께 확인하는 촬영 정보입니다. Request의 메타데이터는 ControlList로 제공되며, FrameBuffer의 FrameMetadata는 촬영 상태·타임스탬프·사용한 바이트 수 등을 담습니다. FrameMetadata의 다른 필드가 유효한지는 촬영 상태에 따라 달라집니다.
블랙 레벨: 빛이 전혀 없을 때도 센서가 내는 기준값입니다. ISP 처리의 첫 단계에서 이 값을 뺍니다.
셰이더: GPU에서 실행되는 작은 프로그램입니다. 소프트웨어 ISP는 디베이어와 색 보정을 GPU 셰이더로 수행할 수 있습니다.
소프트웨어 ISP: 하드웨어 ISP가 없는 장치에서 CPU나 GPU로 ISP 처리를 대신하는 libcamera 구성 요소입니다. 소스에서는 software_isp, softisp라는 이름을 씁니다.
왜곡 보정: 렌즈 때문에 휘어진 영상을 곧게 펴는 처리입니다. RKISP1 파이프라인은 DW100 장치에 좌표 표(vertex map)를 넣어 수행합니다.
컨트롤 정보 맵: 카메라에서 사용할 제어 항목과 범위를 나타내는 정보입니다. 요청의 컨트롤 목록은 해당 카메라의 정보 맵을 참조해야 합니다.
튜닝 파일: 센서와 플랫폼별 알고리즘 매개변수(보정 표, 색 행렬 등)를 담은 YAML 파일입니다. IPA가 시작할 때 읽습니다.
프레임 버퍼: 영상 데이터를 저장할 메모리 영역을 나타내는 FrameBuffer 객체입니다. 각 메모리 평면의 파일 기술자·오프셋·길이와 프레임별 메타데이터를 제공합니다. 촬영 성공·오류·취소에 따라 데이터와 메타데이터의 유효 범위가 달라집니다.
프록시: IPA 모듈을 직접 부르지 않고, 같은 인터페이스로 호출을 받아 IPA 스레드나 별도 프로세스로 전달하는 대리 객체입니다. 빌드할 때 mojom 정의에서 자동 생성됩니다.
활성 스트림: 현재 카메라 구성에 연결된 Stream입니다. 요청 버퍼가 다른 구성의 스트림을 가리키면 제출 검사에서 거절됩니다.
기능·강점·연동 조건을 판단하려면 For Vendor에서, 처음 구조를 배우거나 다른 팀의 코드를 수정하려면 For Developer에서 시작하세요.
